scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Scott Wagner and I'm 80. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Mr. Wagner, I'm sorry to hear about the trouble with your billing while you were away. I can certainly look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide the email address associated with your account and your account number?
Sure, the email is scott.wagner@email.com and my account number is 8849201.
Thank you. Just to verify, could you please confirm your full billing address on file?
Yes, it's 123 Maple Street, Springfield, IL 62704.

Thanks for that. I see your account here. Per our standard terms of service, refunds are typically limited to a 30-day window from the date of the charge. Since you are four days past that, I'm not entirely sure if the system will allow me to process this automatically.
I understand the policy, but given the circumstances, is there any flexibility? It’s only a few days.

I understand your position. Because this is outside the standard window, I am going to escalate this to our billing specialist team who has the authority to grant one-time exceptions for travel-related delays. I have opened a case for you, and they will review it within 48 hours.

escalation_reason: The refund request falls outside the standard 30-day policy window, requiring manual review by the billing specialist team for a potential exception.
